doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Original songs and the record business
title: Why labels resist an all-original record
summary: Asked about an album of originals, he says one label did not take to one, and he prefers sneaking originals onto records.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: When you worked, you’ve been with a couple of different record labels. If you went to them and said we would like to do a CD of all original material, what would they respond?

We did try to do one, for one of the labels. And it wasn’t received well. And I think we were, the funny part was we were three songs off. We had a bunch of good songs and then there were a couple at the end of the list that weren’t so hot. And so we literally in like a day or two came up with three songs to replace those but the die was cast as it were. But it’s something that — I like sneaking them on the records as opposed to a whole record just for familiarity’s sake. But there’s two on the Sinatra and Jobim record, there’s one called “She’s So Sensitive” and “Canto Casual” just a simple tune. And those got well reviewed. So we’re just slowly working our way up to it. I wouldn’t mind doing it myself. It’s got to be — we’ve got to really — we have a couple of good ones in the pipeline.
